name: partial_summation_bound325
math: If every initial partial sum of z through N has norm at most B, the norm of the sum of w times z is at most B times the absolute final weight plus its discrete total variation.

name: unimodal_variation_bound325
math: For nonnegative weights with a peak at p below N, increasing before p and decreasing after p, the absolute final weight plus discrete variation is at most twice the weight at p.

name: unimodal_partial_sum_bound325
math: For those unimodal weights and nonnegative B bounding every partial sum of z through N, the weighted sum norm is at most twice B times the peak weight.

name: weighted_phase_variation325
math: At positive nearest integer distance d of alpha, weighted interval phases have norm at most the endpoint plus variation times the minimum of N and one over twice d.

name: unimodal_phase_bound325
math: For a nonnegative unimodal weight and positive nearest integer distance d, the interval phase norm is at most twice the peak times the minimum of N and one over twice d.
instance: w = 1, alpha = 1/4, M = 3, N = 8 and p = 0

name: eta2_monotone_left325
math: Eta2 is nondecreasing on the whole interval up to one half, including its zero extension.

name: eta2_antitone_right325
math: Eta2 is nonincreasing on the whole interval from one half onward, including its zero extension.

name: eta2_between325
math: For a at most b at most c, eta2 at b is at least the smaller of eta2 at a and eta2 at c.

name: sampled_weight_phase_bound325
math: Let w be nonnegative and bounded by H, with every middle value at least the smaller endpoint value. For nondecreasing samples t and positive nearest integer distance d, the weighted interval phase norm is at most twice H times the minimum of N and one over twice d.
instance: w = 1, t = 0, H = 1, alpha = 1/4, M = 3 and N = 8

name: eta2_sampled_phase_bound325
math: For nondecreasing samples t and positive nearest integer distance d, the eta2 weighted interval phase norm is at most eight log 2 times the minimum of N and one over twice d.

name: eta2rho_monotone_left325
math: For rho at least four, eta2rho is nondecreasing up to one half.

name: eta2rho_antitone_right325
math: For rho at least four, eta2rho is nonincreasing from one half onward.

name: eta2rho_between325
math: For rho at least four and a at most b at most c, eta2rho at b is at least the smaller endpoint value.

name: eta2rho_sampled_phase_bound325
math: For rho at least four, nondecreasing samples t and positive nearest integer distance d, the logarithmic weighted phase norm is at most eight log 2 times log rho times the minimum of N and one over twice d.
instance: rho = 4, t = 1/2, alpha = 1/4, M = 3 and N = 8

name: odd_phase_norm325
math: Removing the constant unit phase from the first N odd phases leaves a consecutive phase sum with doubled frequency and the same norm.

name: odd_eta2_phase_bound325
math: For nonnegative s and positive nearest integer distance d of twice alpha, the first N odd eta2 weighted phases have norm at most eight log 2 times the minimum of N and one over twice d.

name: odd_log_eta2_phase_bound325
math: For positive m and x at least four m, let d be the positive nearest integer distance of twice alpha m. The first N odd phases weighted by log n times eta2 of mn over x have norm at most eight log 2 times log of x over m times the minimum of N and one over twice d.

name: eta2_sampled_length_bound325
math: For arbitrary real samples and frequencies, the eta2 weighted interval phase norm is at most four log 2 times N.

name: minor_odd_eta2_block325
math: Under MinorHyp, let s lie in q consecutive natural numbers below Q over two. The sum over s of the norms of N odd eta2 weighted phases is at most eight log 2 times the minimum of the cardinality of s times N and N plus twice q times one plus log q. The exceptional residue is included.

name: coprimeMu_multiplicative
math: The Mobius function restricted to integers coprime to q is multiplicative.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: coprimeMu_zeta_prime_pow
math: The divisor transform of the restricted Mobius function at p to the power k plus one is one if p divides q and zero otherwise, for prime p.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: coprimeMu_zeta_values
math: At every natural integer the divisor transform of the restricted Mobius function is zero or one.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: coprimeMu_abs
math: Every restricted Mobius coefficient has absolute value at most one.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: coprimeMu_zeta_zero_of_coprime
math: The divisor transform vanishes at each integer other than one that is coprime to q.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: coprimeMu_complement_bound
math: At every integer other than one, the divisor transform plus the absolute restricted coefficient is at most one.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: coprimeMu_floor_sum
math: The sum of the divisor transform through N equals the sum of the restricted coefficients times the integer quotient of N by the index.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: reciprocal_floor_identity
math: N times the reciprocal weighted sum of f through N equals its floor weighted sum plus its remainder weighted sum divided by the index.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: coprime_mobius_reciprocal_bound
math: For every natural q and N, the absolute reciprocal sum of restricted Mobius coefficients from one through N is at most one.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: granville_ramare_10_2
math: For every real x and natural q, the absolute sum of the quotients mu n divided by n from one through floor x with n coprime to q is at most one. Real endpoints below one give an empty sum.
page: GR96 preprint 42 Lemma 10.2 and Helfgott 7 equation 2.7

name: first_approximation_endpoint325
math: At x = 2.16e20, alpha = 1/54000000000000, a = 1, q = 27000000000000 and delta = 0 satisfy MinorHyp and the strict large denominator condition.
instance: The displayed point satisfies every hypothesis jointly

name: reset_disjunction_counterexample325
math: For that alpha, numerator zero, denominator one and delta = 8000000 give a valid reset approximation with Q = x to the two thirds divided by 500 square root 6. Neither q greater than y nor absolute delta q greater than eight y holds. The latter is equality.
instance: x = 2.16e20 and the displayed two approximations

name: parameter_product325
math: For positive x, U times V equals 500 square root 6 divided by three times x to the two thirds.

name: parameter_product_exceeds_short_range325
math: For positive x, the product U V exceeds half of the original Q. The short block estimate alone does not cover the full coefficient range.

name: first_denominator_exceeds_reset325
math: At x = 2.16e20, the reset Q is strictly below the valid first denominator 27000000000000.
